newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-HULL NETS 500TH GOAL.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-HULL NETS 500TH GOAL.

text.p: Brett Hull scored his 26th career hat trick and became the 24th player in NHL history to score 500 goals, as the St. Louis Blues beat the Los Angeles Kings 7-4 on Sunday.

After scoring in each of the first two periods, Hull was credited with his 500th career goal 20 seconds into the third. His slap shot from the edge of the slot hit teammate Stephane Matteau and bounced past goaltender Stephane Fiset.
Replays clearly showed the puck hit Matteau. Hull's goal stood for about five minutes until he huddled with off-ice officials and Matteau was credited with the tally.
"I was telling Matty (Matteau) I can't take that, it's your goal," Hull said. "Let's go get another."
But midway through the period, Hull rifled a slap shot from the right faceoff circle through Fiset's pads for the milestone goal.
"I had been thinking about it all year," Hull said. "To be be put among those players who have done it and to have done it here at home ... is really something."
In Chicago, Eric Lindros scored twice in a 48-second span of the second period as the Philadelphia Flyers lost their shutout streak, but rallied for a 2-2 tie with the Chicago Blackhawks.

Philadelphia set a club record by shutting out its previous four opponents, but Chicago's Sergei Krivokrasov beat goaltender Garth Snow 2:38 into the first period to end the streak at 265 minutes, eight seconds.
Tony Amonte added his 22nd goal at 16:08 to stake the Blackhawks to a 2-0 lead for the second time in three games.

In Edmonton, Brendan Shanahan, Vyacheslav Kozlov and Jamie Pushor scored second-period goals and Chris Osgood made 32 saves as the Detroit Red Wings continued their dominance of the Edmonton Oilers with a 6-2 win.
Detroit snapped a three-game winless streak, and the Oilers now are winless in their last six (0-3-3).
"We were not playing well," Shanahan said. "We only had one point to show for three games on this trip, so we were looking for something positive to go into the Christmas break with."

In New York, Mark Messier had two goals and two assists and Alexei Kovalev and Niklas Sundstrom also scored twice, leading the red-hot New York Rangers to their fifth straight win, a 7-3 rout of the first-place Florida Panthers.
New York is unbeaten in 12 of its last 13 games (11-1-1).
"We have been beating teams with not good records and tonight we beat one of the best teams in the league," Messier said.
Former Ranger Ray Sheppard had his second hat trick of the season for Florida.
In Phoenix, German Titov recorded his second career hat trick and Theo Fleury added a goal and two assists to power the Calgary Flames to a 7-2 victory over the Phoenix Coyotes.
Todd Hlushko, Jarome Iginla and Ronnie Stern also scored and Robert Reichel had three assists for the Flames, who snapped a three-game winless streak and won for just the third time in 11 games.
Keith Tkachuk and Darrin Shannon scored for the Coyotes.
